summary: Iteration 8 (frontend-only): verified the new LiveKit network-quality badge on participant cards. Live-tested on preview URL (https://realtime-voice-hub-6.preview.emergentagent.com). Admin (Bob) solo view: 1 card, 1 badge. Two-party session (Bob admin + Alice user in separate browser contexts): BOTH views render 2 cards and 2 badges with data-testid='participant-quality-<identity>', data-quality='good', literal text 'Good', and dot class 'bg-[#4C7D5B]' (green) — matches spec. Code review confirms: build() adds connectionQuality with 'unknown' fallback (line 121), RoomEvent.ConnectionQualityChanged bound to refreshParticipants (line 340), getQuality() mapping excellent/good->good #4C7D5B, poor->weak #E5B93B, default(lost/unknown)->poor #C84C4C (lines 732-742), badge rendered in the top-right stack above Host/Mic badges (lines 765-786), testIds.js exposes participantQualityPrefix. Regression checks passed: admin/user section split, Recent Speakers strip (host-only by design), PTT bar, muted card state (data-state='muted', red), host controls (Mic/Mute/Kick) on member card. Backend light check: /api/auth/login returns tokens for owner (platform_owner), admin (room_admin), user (user) — all 200.

integration_issues.issue: Could NOT be exercised at runtime: applied CDP network throttling (2s latency, 8kbps) for 30s on Alice's session and LiveKit ConnectionQuality never left 'excellent/good' (WebRTC media path is not throttled by CDP). The 'Weak' (#E5B93B) and 'Poor' (#C84C4C) states are verified by code review + DOM attribute injection only, not by a real LiveKit event. Not a defect, just untested-at-runtime coverage.

design_issues.screen: Room — participant grid (carried over from iteration_7, still open)
issues: gridAutoRows 1fr still stretches a single member/user card to ~630px tall (large solid red block, name pinned to the bottom, badge floating far from the name). This makes the new quality badge visually detached from the participant it describes.

Green quality dot (#4C7D5B) sitting inside a red muted card (#C84C4C) is low-contrast/confusing; the uppercase 'GOOD' text label mitigates it, but consider a white/neutral dot border or a lighter pill background on colored cards.

action_items: Optional: cap participant card height (or vertically centre content) when only 1-2 cards are visible so the quality badge stays adjacent to the name (open since iteration_7).
Optional: improve quality-dot contrast on colored (muted/speaking) cards.
critical_code_review_comments: RoomPage.jsx is 935 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline; consider extracting renderCard/getQuality/getCardState into components/room/*.jsx.

getQuality() is defined inside the render IIFE, so it is re-created on every render (also every 500ms nowTick). Harmless but better hoisted to module scope as a pure helper (and it would then be unit-testable, which would cover the weak/poor mapping that cannot be exercised via a real LiveKit event).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of testable badge assertions (good-level only; weak/poor not reproducible at runtime)

Multi-participant room testing pattern that works: log Bob in on `page`, then create a second browser context (page.context.browser.new_context()) for Alice so tokens don't collide; admin path = login -> admin-enter-room-button -> room-enter-button, user path = login -> room-enter-button. rca_of_the_issue: No defect found in the iteration_8 feature. The only unverified area (weak/poor levels) is due to headless-Chrome/CDP not throttling the WebRTC media path, so LiveKit never reports degraded ConnectionQuality.
